chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Qasim from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the person in ihram who covered his head unintentionally. He said: He should remove the head-cover from his head, say the Talbiyah, and there is no penalty upon him.

key_terms.الْقِنَاعَ: The head-cover (specifically a cloth or garment placed on the head)
key_terms.الْمُحْرِمِ: The person in the state of ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.يُلَبِّي: He says the Talbiyah (the declaration of readiness to meet God)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a pilgrim accidentally covers their head during Hajj?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that unintentional head covering during Ihram incurs no expiation (*damm*), emphasizing the principle of *al-yaqin la yuzalu bi-shakk* (certainty is not removed by doubt) in ritual purity. This ruling distinguishes between forgetful acts, which are excused, and intentional violations, which require compensation, reflecting the Shia juristic focus on ease (*taysir*) in pilgrimage rites. The instruction to simply remove the covering and renew the *Talbiyah* underscores the continuity of the pilgrim's state without the need for complex ritual resets.
